The proposed solution is **incorrect**. 

For any code containing the all-ones codeword (which Reed-Solomon and Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon codes do when $t \ge 1$), the code satisfies $C \subseteq C^2$, and powers of non-constant evaluation polynomials (e.g., $1, x, x^2, \dots, x^{2t-2}$) show that the dimension of the Schur square must be strictly greater than $t$ (in the classical case $s=1$, the dimension of the Schur square is $2t - 1 > t$ for $t \ge 2s \ge 2$). It cannot be equal to $t$.

VERDICT: REJECT
